description: An Erling Haaland double helped extend City’s winning start to seven – a Premier League record for Enzo Maresca – in their 3-2 victory over Ipswich
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: An Erling Haaland double helped extend City’s winning start to seven – a Premier League record for Enzo Maresca – in their 3-2 victory over Ipswich
Content: Erling Haaland slots home Manchester City’s third goal against Ipswich.Photograph: Dave Thompson/APView image in fullscreenErling Haaland slots home Manchester City’s third goal against Ipswich.Photograph: Dave Thompson/APPremier LeagueHaaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat IpswichWill Unwinat the Etihad StadiumSat 17 Oct 2026 12.08 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 17.23 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being foundto have breached financial rules. Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming.Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nineRead more“I didn’t expect to win seven out of seven, but we are working well,” Maresca said. “This is the most important thing.”Victory came at a cost as Haaland and AntoineSemenyo limped off at full-time, in addition to Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly suffering injuries, although Maresca was left unsure of the severity as City prepare to host AEK Athens on Tuesday.If City have felt like it has been their backs against the wall for the past few weeks, it was Ipswich’s turn. Gary O’Neil put 11 men behind the ball whenever the hosts ventured over the halfway line as City enjoyed 90% possession in the opening quarter-hour, but without truly threatening as they struggled to find space in the lowest of blocks, expertly organised and fully disciplined.Maresca had made six changes to refresh the side and it took time to understand one another’s rhythm, with Ayyoub Bouaddi creating it from defensive midfield in another mature performance from the teenager making his firstPremier Leaguestart.View image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca has guided Manchester City a record seven-match winning start in the Premier League.Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty ImagesIt was inevitable what was coming as there was irrefutable evidence that City were dominant.As at Anfield, Jérémy Doku was a key instigator, showing mesmeric skill on the left of the area before finding Foden to sweep home for his first goal since mid-December.“I know him from years ago, for me he’s one of the best Premier League players,” Maresca said. “Since day one, it’s my duty to help him to be again one of the best players. I’m very happy for his goal and hopefully it can be just the beginning of many goals and many good performances.”There was an element of pantomime around the ground from the booing of the Premier League anthem, the singalongs and inflatables. It was fitting Marc Guéhi did not know Maeda was behind him, allowing the Ipswich man to latch on to a sublime curved through ball from Abdoul Ouattara and equalise two minutes after the opener.Quick GuideManchester City 3-2 Ipswich key factsShow• With Manchester City maintaining their 100% record, Enzo Maresca isthe first manager to win his first sevenPremier League games in charge of a team.• Manchester City are  the third team to wintheir opening seven gamesof a Premier League season, afterLiverpool in 2019-20(first 8) andChelsea in 2005-06(first 9).• Erling Haaland (pictured) has now scored100 non-penalty goalsin the Premier League, reaching this milestonein fewer appearancesthan any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances, by Alan Shearer in 1996.OptaPhotograph: Martin Rickett/PAWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.After a missed chance, Haaland showed it is possible to get a better result second time around, making the most of Kovacic becoming an auxiliary winger. The header lacked power, but Christian Walton could not keep it out, palming the ball from one hand to the other and into the net before Haaland was serenaded with the clap of bananas.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCity found themselves stuck in a lull, unable to prise open Ipswich, instead having to bide their time. It was a test of patience and a sweeping move upfield concluded with a precision pass from Iliman Ndiaye and an aggressive finish from Haaland, who was later denied a hat-trick by the video assistant referee.View image in fullscreenManchester City fans have gone back to more innocent times with their inflatable bananas.Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesFarai Hallam reviewed footage of Guéhi taking out Abdul Fatawu in the area and Flemming did the rest in the 90th minute, as reward for an impressive team performance, leaving O’Neil upset Ipswich departed with nothing.“They’re an incredible group,” he said. “Players giving everything. It’s a privilege to stand there and represent them because they’re an incredible group.”City were left to complain about a Premier League official’s decision when 12 minutes was added on, with few knowing why, but this result will not be questioned.Maresca called on his team to make their own noise while a cacophony swirls around them, but on-pitch success will not speak louder while what is happening off it is unresolved. The fans sang about relegation and trips to Stockport, embracing a dark situation with humour to match.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CityIpswich Townmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Daniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO title | Boxing | The Guardian
description: Daniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in the second round of their WBO world title fight as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet
Author: Donald McRae
Headline: Daniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in the second round of their WBO world title fight as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet
Content: Daniel Dubois lands a blow on Fabio Wardley at the O2 Arena.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois lands a blow on Fabio Wardley at the O2 Arena.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersBoxingDaniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO titleDubois underlines status as Britain’s leading heavyweightWardley’s corner throw in the towel in second roundDonald McRaeat the O2 ArenaSat 17 Oct 2026 18.30 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDaniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in their WBO world title fight on Saturday night as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet with this crushing victory. This was the second time in five months that Dubois has defeated Wardley but, after theirfight of the year contender in May, he unleashed a shockingly one-sided shellacking.Daniel Dubois knocks out Fabio Wardley to retain WBO heavyweight title – live reactionRead moreAfter two minutes and 21 seconds of round two, Wardley was rescued from the bludgeoning fists of Dubois by the referee, just as the fluttering white towel of his trainer, Ben Davison, sailed over the ropes in surrender. Davison had been on the brink of throwing in the towel at the very end of the opening round but the bell sounded to end a disastrous first three minutes for Wardley. He was dropped heavily after just 17 seconds as Dubois landed a left cross followed by a pulverising right hand.It was the first time Wardley had been forced to take a count in 23 fights as a professional and he looked suitably stunned. He seemed helpless as Dubois pummelled him around the ring with a thunderous array of mostly unanswered punches. In the last 15 seconds of the round Wardley was pinned in Dubois’ corner as the punishing blows intensified.View image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois overpowers Fabio Wardley in their much-anticipated clash in London.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersHe came out for the second round and, while he threw some wild haymakers and wayward uppercuts, Wardley could not stem the dark tide of punches engulfing him. The end was merciful.Wardley had walked to the ring in a sombre yet purposeful manner but the bridge of his nose still carried a red scar of the deep gash he had suffered when he last shared a ring with Dubois. But he raised his right hand high as soon as he ducked through the ropes. Dubois followed at a much quicker lick as Salt-N-Pepa’s Whatta Man boomed around him. The two men were brought face to face for their final instructions – and carnage ensued soon afterwards.Dubois’ boxing fundamentals are far superior to Wardley’s more crude technique, which lacks a proper grounding in amateur boxing. Wardley used to be a white-collar boxer and his rise to becoming a respected world champion is an unlikely but hugely admirable sporting story. He lost his title and unbeaten record to Dubois in their gripping but also harrowing first fight; and this devastating defeat confirmed the limits of Wardley’s talent.“I had bad intentions from the beginning,” Dubois said. “Our back was against the wall last time – this time we had to go out and show we mean business from the start.”The contest in May took chunks out of Wardley because, despite knocking down Dubois twice in the early rounds, he suffered a horrible pounding for the rest of the bout, which ended in the 11th. He would have been better advised to take a far longer break from boxing than rushing back into a rematch. It can only be hoped that the salutary lessons doled out by Dubois persuade him to change course.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois celebrates retaining his WBO title.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters“It’s never fun to lose – but it is what it is, it’s the name of the game,” Wardley said in his conversational way. “I’ve always taken on the biggest challenges … I tried to adjust some things but it didn’t work tonight.Boxingis a game of fine margins. I didn’t touch the canvas, so there’s a little bit of pride in that.”Wardley is an engaging and intelligent man and he would carve out an impressive career as a boxing analyst on television. It would be far better for his health if he could do his best work in the years to come on the safe side of the ropes.The future for Dubois, in contrast, is much more straightforward. This clinical and decisive performance will propel him towards a potential series of unification contests against Filip Hrgovic and Agit Kabayel, who hold rival versions of the world title. But, as he proved with this utterly dominant performance, Dubois looks a cut above the rest of the heavyweight pack.Explore more on these topicsBoxingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams | Saudi Arabia and sport | The Guardian
description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling
Author: Rob Draper
Headline: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling
Content: Cristiano Ronaldo dons a Saudi scarf after the match against Neftchi Fergana that was delayed by a missile warning.Photograph: ReutersView image in fullscreenCristiano Ronaldo dons a Saudi scarf after the match against Neftchi Fergana that was delayed by a missile warning.Photograph: ReutersSaudi Arabia and sportHouthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreamsA match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stallingRob DraperSat 17 Oct 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 11.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”.Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game wasdelayed by a threat of missile attacksfrom Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after13 people died and more than 300 were woundedby Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport.Fresh concerns over 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia after missile strikes in RiyadhRead moreSaudi Arabia’s hosting of football’s Asian Cup in January and February is being questioned – it insists preparations are on track – and a combination of rapidly changing geopolitics and a reality check being applied to the more quixotic projects means the kingdom’s position in the sporting landscape looks hugely different from a year ago. Golf’s Asian Tour has postponed next month’s Saudi International indefinitely, next month’s cycling urban world championship in Riyadh has been cancelled, the Fifa esports World Cup – which had been due to start on Friday – has been postponed and the Six Kings Slam tennis event, due to be held next week, has been pushed back until late December.View image in fullscreenTyson Fury and Oleksandr Usyk fight in Riyadh in December 2024. Boxing is likely to survive the Saudi sporting cull.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAAlongside thehumiliating collapse of LIV Golf, the planned 2029 Saudi Winter Asian Games has been relocated to Kazakhstan, which has actual mountains with snow. In the football sphere, it has been reported that five proposed new stadiums for the 2034 World Cup may not be built. One of them is the Neom stadium, which was planned with an elevation of 350 metres, after huge cuts to the fantastical city development project known as the Line.In September last year there were signs all might not be what it seemed. At a Washington DC investment thinktank the Newcastle chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan, dressed in suit and tie, very much in sync with the patrician vibe of the event, addressed hedge fund chiefs and entrepreneurs along with the private equity billionaire David Rubenstein.Canelo Álvarez ‘fears nothing’ and will fight in Riyadh despite deadly attacks, Al-Sheikh saysRead moreUnsurprisingly, Newcastle’s Carabao Cup triumph was barely mentioned. Al-Rumayyan was principally there as the chair of Aramco, the Saudi oil company, and as the governor of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), the country’s largest sovereign wealth fund. PIF is chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the de facto ruler of the kingdom and the man accused by US intelligence ofapproving the murder of the journalist Jamal Khashoggi.Al-Rumayyan took time, in between banter about how the result of his golf match with Donald Trump was a “state secret”, to lecture the audience on history and why the need for Saudi to divest from oil was existential“Portugal was one of the richest countries in the world with all the gold that they had,” he said. “And that’s like a disease. That’s what the crown prince always talks about … ‘We have the oil disease.’ We cannot rely only on oil because this will make you more dormant, less active. We have growth in population and we need to find new jobs for new people coming. Seventy-five per cent of Saudis are under the age of 35. We need to give them the quality of life they deserve and find them jobs. We cannot just rely on one commodity. We don’t want to do the same mistakes that [other] great nations have made.”View image in fullscreen‘We cannot just rely on one commodity’: Newcastle’s chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan, has said Saudi Arabia needs to diversify away from oil.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersThe unspoken threat alluded to by al-Rumayyan is that a nation of “dormant” young men in the birthplace of Osama bin Laden could turn to radical Islam, as the 15 Saudi nationals among the 9/11 bombers did. And now there is the prospect that the Houthi missiles and the US war with Iran may jeopardise the best-laid Saudi state plans.“If the war affects the ability of the regime economically – by which I mean [creating] jobs – then potential for unrest grows,” says Christopher Davidson, author of From Sheikhs to Sultanism: Statecraft and Authority in Saudi Arabia and the UAE.“If rulers fail to deliver on jobs for a massive youth bulge, the seductive message of online forums becomes even more compelling for young men.”LIV was part of that shift to leisure investments and was al-Rumayyan’s brainchild, if that’s the correct word for a project that made a reported $6bn (£4.5bn) loss for PIF. Given the country club ambience among his Washington audience, golf was addressed and al-Rumayyan was still talking about wanting to “bring the game of golf back together” and “increasing the share of [revenue] pie”, this being six months before Saudi Arabia pulled the plug on the LIV project, which filed for bankruptcy protection in September.Yet even in Washington al-Rumayyan was strongly hinting that entrepreneurs shouldn’t come asking for money for pet projects unless they could give something back to his country beyond financial returns, explaining that from 2021 PIF had shifted investment back towards Saudi Arabia. “The trigger for us, if we want to deploy capital with asset managers, [is that] we would like to get some of the deployment back to the country [Saudi Arabia] because we need to increase and grow our local content,” al-Rumayyan said. “One of the best ways to do so is direct foreign investment.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe reassuring news for Newcastle is that a trophy investment in the Premier League will survive the overseas investment cull. “They are reducing their spending but I think football is probably ringfenced, given they’re hosting the 2034 World Cup,” says Davidson. “I would imagine the PIF funding [for Newcastle] is secure going forward.” That said, the supporters’ dreams of huge spending will never happen, as most have accepted. In the Saudi Pro League, PIF this year sold a controlling stake in Al-Hilal but it continues to own three others: Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli.PIF clubs’ net transfer spend by season, €m“There is pressure from the very top in Saudi Arabia for PIF to cut some corners,” Davidson says, “and that is accelerating because of the war and more focus on their efforts at domestic economy building.”Boxing too – assuming Saudi is safe for events – will survive the cut and esports, a $38bn slice of PIF and a proven way to divert young men from extremism, could thrive. “They require very little budget but hit an enormous audience,” Davidson says.View image in fullscreenNewcastle are likely to continue to be well funded by the Saudi regime but huge spending will not happen.Photograph: Richard Sellers/PABut a World Cup stadium in the sky, skiing in the desert and futuristic cities are out, as are any more expensive overseas money pits such as LIV. “[Trump’s] Republicans struggling in the midterm election in the USA will factor into what type of sports all the Gulf states will be thinking of investing in,” Davidson says. “LIV was seen as a project closely aligned with Trump’s passions. And that may be reduced if they see the direction [of politics] swinging.”The Saudi Pro League and World Cup 2034, though, are very much still on the agenda, even with fewer stadiums. However, that will be reliant on the cessation of the US-Iran war and the subjugation of Houthi rebels, neither of which is likely to have featured prominently in Ronaldo’s transfer negotiations when he opted to join Al-Nassr for his career sunset in Saudi but suddenly seem very pertinent.PIF has been contacted for comment.Explore more on these topicsSaudi Arabia and sportSport politicsFootball politicsSaudi ArabiafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a  super-club | Europa League | The Guardian
description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically
Content: Sunderland’s Noah Sadiki celebrates scoring against Torreense. Bournemouth and Sunderland are prospering in the Europa League but the price for lively adventures abroad is high domestically.Photograph: Octávio Passos/UEFA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSunderland’s Noah Sadiki celebrates scoring against Torreense. Bournemouth and Sunderland are prospering in the Europa League but the price for lively adventures abroad is high domestically.Photograph: Octávio Passos/UEFA/Getty ImagesInside footballEuropa LeagueEurope is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a  super-clubJonathan WilsonThe four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domesticallySat 17 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 15.02 EDTShareThe sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free.Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.”Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?Read moreThis was everything Sunderland fans could have wished for from their first European away game in 53 years and more. They had seen other fans experience these things, and now they could tick off the checklist: complicated travel to a pretty foreign town they would otherwise never visit, a fussy Albanian referee and a great sense of togetherness and community. There was evenan injury-time winnerfrom, miracle of miracles, Noah Sadiki.Ask any of the 5,000 or so Wearsiders who made the trip to Portugal if the Europa League was worth it and the answer would be unanimous. Bournemouth,Crystal Palaceand Brighton fans would surely say something similar: European football, especially for clubs who are unfamiliar with it, is a joy and an adventure. It generates experiences that will be remembered for ever, and if the cost is that the risk of relegation goes up, that’s a price worth paying. Others at those clubs may see things differently.View image in fullscreenSunderland fans enjoyed a trip they will remember for ever when they played TorreensePhotograph: Paulo Cunha/EPAThe four Premier League clubs involved in the lesser two European competitions play each other on Sunday.Brighton are thriving; the other three are not. Palace were 12th before the weekend fixtures but not playing well. Bournemouth against Sunderland is a battle of third- and fourth-bottom. Whether the Europa League football can yet be blamed is debatable.Brighton surely can’t be bucking the trendjust because of the lesser demands of the Conference League. Thursday’s was only the second round of Europa League league games, and the clubs involved bypassed a round of the Carabao Cup; fatigue may come but it shouldn’t be an issue yet.There are other factors at play. Sunderland have already played Manchester City, Arsenal, Brighton and Brentford, the top four going into this weekend. They could easily have been a couple of goals up by half-time at Brentford. They missed a penalty to go ahead against Arsenal. They registered an xG of 2.72 inlosing 5-3 at Manchester City. Only in thedefeat to Brightonlast weekend have they really disappointed. In the equivalent six games last season (substituting Ipswich for Burnley), Sunderland took only one point; in that sense, they are actually three points better off this campaign.But that can’t alter the fact that four points from six games leaves them beginning to fret. There is pressure on this next run of fixtures: afterBournemouth, they are home to Leeds, then away to Coventry. Sunderland’s transfer business left a major question on the right of the forward line that has yet to be resolved. A lack of depth in certain areas has been exposed by injuries to Brian Brobbey and Habib Diarra, although both players were on the bench on Thursday.Bournemouth have also lost key players to injury. Eli JuniorKroupi, who scored 13 league goals last season, has not played this campaign. Neither has Amine Adli, although he came off the bench on Thursday, as did Justin Kluivert, who had been out for a month. Most damagingly of all, perhaps, after impressing for England against Croatia,Alex Scott has been ruled outwith a thigh injury.The transition away from Andoni Iraola was always likely to be disruptive and, while Saturday’s5-1 defeat at Chelseawas a jolt, their other losses this season wereto Manchester CityandLiverpool. There has been a sense of margins going against them, of draws that might have been wins. The concern, as with Sunderland, comes if that affects morale, and decent displays that have yielded disappointing results curdle into disappointing performances.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenÁlvaro Rodríguez scores Bournemouth’s third goal against Sturm Graz, but they have found domestic assignments tougher.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersPalace are in a slightly different position. Other than City, their fixture list has been relatively kind. Seven points from six games would constitute comfortable survival if extrapolated over the season as a whole, but Opta’s expected points table, which has Bournemouth ninth andSunderland10th, has them 18th. A new manager is settling in, Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Múñoz were sold over the summer, while Jean-Philippe Mateta hasn’t played since the opening weekend.For none of those three sides can unsettled starts be blamed entirely or even primarily on Europe. That said, the evidence is clear: over the past five years, teams who did not play in Europe the previous season see their league position fall when they do play in Europe: Palace dropped from 12th to 15th, Nottingham Forest from seventh to 16th, Newcastle from fifth to 12th, Brighton from sixth to 11th, West Ham from sixth to seventh. Of those examples, only Forest even came vaguely close to relegation, but the fear nags away.Although winning theEuropa Leaguewould bring the vast rewards of Champions League football, losing in the final would probably bring in not much more than £20m for a Premier League club, plus gate receipts and whatever intangible benefits there might be from increased exposure. To put that in context, that’s roughly the difference between finishing ninth and 14th in the Premier League.Which is to say that while fans revel in trips to Milan, Prague or Lyon, for club executives a few nice mini-breaks do not balance out the potential financial headaches.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueInside footballSunderlandCrystal PalaceBournemouthConference LeagueBrighton & Hove AlbioncommentShareReuse this content

title: Manzambi maintains Aston Villa progress with win to seal dismal week for Newcastle | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Johan Manzambi’s first-half goal earned Aston Villa a 1-0 Premier League victory at St James’ Park to complete a dismal week for Newcastle
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Johan Manzambi’s first-half goal earned Aston Villa a 1-0 Premier League victory at St James’ Park to complete a dismal week for Newcastle
Content: Johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa ahead in the first half.Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJohan Manzambi heads Aston Villa ahead in the first half.Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueManzambi maintains Aston Villa progress with win to seal dismal week for NewcastleLouise Taylorat St James' ParkSat 17 Oct 2026 14.38 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 16.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere is a reason why Aston Villa were so desperate to hijack Johan Manzambi’s proposed summer move from Freiburg to Newcastle. The tall, quick, tricky, clever and perfectly balanced 21-year-old Switzerland attacking midfielder looked worth every penny ofthe record £50m plus feeVilla ended up paying and he duly delighted in showing Tynesiders what they missed.For Newcastle and their disconsolate manager, Matthias Jaissle, there was a cruel irony that Manzambi ended up heading the winner on a day when the Premier League’s CEO, Richard Masters, was in the directors’ box to watch arguably the two teams most affected by the spending rules imposed during his tenure.Newcastle v Aston Villa: Premier League – liveRead moreThose regulations have turned Unai Emery into a master of reinvention atAston Villabut, in the league at least, the Spaniard’s latest rebuild has been slow to click cleanly into place. On the evidence of their fourth win in five games in all competitions, that just might be changing.While Villa kicked off having won only once in the league this season, Newcastle sought redemption after last Monday night’schastening 4-1 defeatat Coventry.Emery, who changed his mind about taking charge of Newcastle before Eddie Howe took the job, said: “It was a tough match but it was very important to win after our poor start. But we set a high standard.”Jaissle, whose team are level on points with Villa but faces an appreciably tougher reconstruction project, was left to reflect on his “frustration” and blamed his young team’s decision making. But Newcastle’s manager was also sanguine. “Big names left the club in the summer so for sure, we knew it would be challenging,” he said. “That’s not an excuse, we have to learn fast.”View image in fullscreenJohan Manzambi strikes a pose after scoring the winner.Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesThere has always been a certain edge between these teams and Jarred Gillett issued two first-half yellow cards in quick succession. First Joelinton lunged in, two-footed, on Manzambi and then Sven Botman was guilty of another reckless challenge, two-footed and over the ball, on the dangerous Nicolas Jackson.A video assistant referee check ensued but, after lengthy deliberation, it was decided the original decision was correct and Botman’s yellow did not require upgrading to a red. The Newcastle centre-half was probably a little fortunate. “It was so high it nearly broke my leg,” said Jackson. “But I’m OK; it’s part of football.”Joelinton, meanwhile, has now been booked in each of the two games he has been involved in since returning from injury as a substitute at Coventry.Plus ça change.The elegantly impressive Manzambi, seemingly electrically powered, exerted the best sort of revenge on the Brazilian when he gave Emery’s side the lead. That goal arrived in the 36th minute and involved an unmarked Manzambi – a creator brilliant at drifting into space – ghosting away from Malick Thiaw before meeting João Gomes’s splendid cross with a tremendous header.Newcastle suddenly looked extremely vulnerable but they were reprieved when Emiliano Buendía’s shot rebounded off the inside of a post and deflected off LukasHornicek’s back before eventually being cleared by Lewis Hall. Once again, Hall was Jaissle’s best player.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenUnai Emery secured his 100th Premier League victory but it was another game to forget for Matthias Jaissle.Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesIt was all too easy to see why Newcastle have now gone 13 Premier League home games without a clean sheet, equalling an unwanted record set in 1998-99.Jaissle’s frustration surfaced itself as he exchanged words with Emery after an altercation involving Alysson and Hornicek and subsequently looked suitably downcast as his side were booed off at half-time.Those home fans were not relishing the sight of Villa’s forward repeatedly accelerating behind the sometimes dangerously high home backline.Quick GuideNewcastle 0-1 Aston Villa key factsShow• Newcastle United are nowwithout a home clean sheetin each of their last 16 games in all competitions; it's the longest run in their history.• Yoane Wissa’s seven shots on goal withnone on targetis the most by a player in a Premier League game since Newcastle teammate Harvey Barnes against Brentford in April 2025 (also 7).• Unai Emery (pictured) has earned his100th Premier League win as a manager, doing so in his 197th game in the competition (D44 L53), only eight managers have done so in fewer games in the competition’s history.OptaPhotograph: Ed Sykes/REUTERSWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Zion Suzuki had been rather underemployed but a goalkeeper briefly courted by Newcastle in the summer opened the second half by making a superlative flying save to keep Botman’s high velocity strike out. It was Newcastle’s sole shot on target.The Villa substitute Ross Barkley almost showed Jaissle’s players how to do it when he would have scored with his first touch had Hornicek not dived smartly to turn his blistering shot around a post.Although Newcastle’s manager sent Dan Burn on for the closing minutes – as a striker – nothing was going to come between Emery and his 100th Premier League win.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueNewcastle UnitedAston Villamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Pressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first win | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Alex Iwobi’s first-half goal gave Fulham a 1-0 win against Hull, despite Ryan Sessegnon’s late red card, to lift them off the bottom
Author: Billy Munday
Headline: Alex Iwobi’s first-half goal gave Fulham a 1-0 win against Hull, despite Ryan Sessegnon’s late red card, to lift them off the bottom
Content: Fulham’s Alex Iwobi (centre) celebrates scoring the winner.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFulham’s Alex Iwobi (centre) celebrates scoring the winner.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesPremier LeaguePressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first winBilly Mundayat Craven CottageSat 17 Oct 2026 12.08 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 14.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was not until his post-match lap of the pitch that Álvaro Arbeloa allowed himself a smile. After an uncomfortable week whenhis future was being called into question, the former Real Madrid manager has a Premier League win under his belt at the seventh attempt, lifting his side off the foot of the table. But it is not a win without caveats.Alex Iwobi’s goal in the first half should have been one of many, with the Nigeria winger among those guilty of missing gilt-edge chances. Gonzalo García, who has not scored in the league since the opening weekend of the season, headed against the crossbar from close range in the second half.Fulham ended with 10 men after Ryan Sessegnon’s red card in stoppage time, but it did not matter against a toothless Hull side, who are now winless in five.Haaland helps extend record start for Maresca as Manchester City defeat IpswichRead moreWith Fulham also a goal up againstIpswich last SaturdayandManchester Unitedhere before the international break before dropping vital points, you could forgive Arbeloa for the stern expression he wore as his team continued to pass up opportunities.“I saw this movie before,” he said. “I didn’t have the feeling we were in danger, but in football you never know. In one second, any team can score.“It is so important to get the chances [converted] because you want to play the last minutes with a little more calm. It’s better to win 2-0 than 1-0, even in a game like that where we were a much better team.”This was a sentiment shared by Hull, whose lack of quality at either end of the pitch was another caveat. “That was the worst performance since I’m here,” said their head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, who is in danger of a promising start fizzling out. “You see in every challenge, they were stronger. Every challenge, they ate us alive.”View image in fullscreenReferee Chris Kavanagh shows a red card to Ryan Sessegnon (left) of Fulham after his foul on Robinio Vaz.Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesThis was the type of performance Fulham would have expected when it appointed Arbeloa as Marco Silva’s successor in the summer. It was a move designed to bring a more entertaining style to Craven Cottage after four years ofPremier Leaguestability in midtable – the Spaniard brought five members of staff with him from Real Madrid and three players.There was plenty of creativity on show against Hull, especially from the wingers Iwobi and Oscar Bobb. They started fast, with Iwobi sending a curling shot on to the roof of the net from the left and Bobb a constant threat on the right.It was from an attack down the right that Fulham produced their winner. Hull’s left wing-back, Brooke Norton-Cuffy, held off Josh King, but failed to clear and Sander Berge poked the ball into Iwobi’s path. His first-time shot should not have troubled the goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, but it squirmed under his rolling dive at the near post after coming through a crowd of bodies.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenFulham’s Alex Iwobi (centre) scores the only goal of the game.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAJakirovic needed to find answers at half-time and he replaced the centre-back Lucas Herrington, who had been booked for one of his fouls on the elusive King, with the midfielder Tim Iroegbunam. After a bright breakthrough season in the first team, the 19-year-old King is expected to push on. He was allowed to roam against Hull’s low block and after neatly combining with Shea Charles should have doubled their lead, but his low shot was too close to Tzolakis.A smart turn from King away from Semi Ajayi preceded a chance that Iwobi, with time and the whole goal to aim at, should have buried, but he telegraphed his low effort for Tzolakis to read and smother. García was unmarked at the back post when he headed Iwobi’s cross against the bar, but Hull provided such little threat that what could have been a nervy ending, especially after Sessegnon’s stoppage-time dismissal for leaving his studs on Robinio Vaz’s achilles, was anything but.With the pressure now relieved a little and his ideas evidently translating to his players, will the often stoney-faced Arbeloa feel more relaxed at training? “I always try to smile,” he said. “Even when you are losing, it’s even more important that you try to smile.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueFulhamHull Citymatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Alexander Isak scored Liverpool’s winner in their 2-1 victory at Brentford, who had Yehor Yarmolyuk sent off at 1-0 up and Vitaly Janelt later saw red
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Alexander Isak scored Liverpool’s winner in their 2-1 victory at Brentford, who had Yehor Yarmolyuk sent off at 1-0 up and Vitaly Janelt later saw red
Content: Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola celebrate Liverpool’s winner.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak and Bradley Barcola celebrate Liverpool’s winner.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueIsak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nineJacob Steinbergat the Gtech Community StadiumSat 17 Oct 2026 12.21 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 14.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIf Liverpool’s spluttering forwards end up remembering this as the day when their luck turned then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. This was a game with a very clear before and after.Andoni Iraola will hope surviving one of the toughest tests thePremier Leaguehas to offer is a sign his methods are starting to work, but Liverpool’s manager will not forget it was a very different contest after Yarmolyuk’s red card for a butt on Jérémy Jacquet left Brentford trying to defend a 1-0 lead with 10 men for the entire second half.Haaland helps extend record start for Maresca as Manchester City defeat IpswichRead moreBrentford, who later lost Vitaly Janelt to a second yellow card, could not hold out. They raged at John Brooks’s officiating after their unbeaten start ended, but they had only themselves to blame after tumbling out of the top four.Brentfordpressed the self-destruct button when they had Liverpool on the ropes. Yarmolyuk was never going to get away it in the video assistant referee era and Liverpool made the midfielder pay.Iraola was delighted with how an attack worth close to £400m made the numerical advantage count after half-time. Most important was a telling contribution from Florian Wirtz. The £100m signing has struggled withthe responsibility of playing as Liverpool’s No 10since joining from Bayer Leverkusen, but this time he was decisive. The clever pass to release Victor Muñoz for a sharp equaliser was his second assist of the season and was followed by Bradley Barcola creating a goal for the first time sincehis move for an initial £106mfrom Paris Saint-Germain, the French winger’s header teeing up Alexander Isak to complete the turnaround in the 70th minute and lift Liverpool into fifth place.The challenge is to push on. Isak’s Liverpool career has been stop-start since his£125m move from Newcastle, injuries holding the forward back. The Spaniard was critical of some sloppy finishing from Barcola, but was readier to dish out the praise for Wirtz’s intelligence in tight spaces in the second half. It feels significant that both of Wirtz’s assists have come for Muñoz.“A good battle today,” Iraola said before switching focus to Barcola and Wirtz. “Both had a lot of influence. Bradley and Flo, they are players that against 10 men are lovely to have.”There was not much between the sides before Yarmolyuk’s rush of blood to the head. Isak returned after missinglast week’s defeat to Manchester Cityand Liverpool shaded the early openings. Barcola almost punished an error from Janelt, only to miss a chance to build onhis midweek hat-trick against LASK. Isak nodded over from a good position.Pressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first winRead moreBrentford responded with a series of fast breaks and Liverpool had to be strong. They looked readier for the threat posed by Brentford than whenthey folded in this fixtureunder Arne Slot 12 months ago. Jacquet, quietly impressive in central defence, made a crucial tackle to deny Igor Thiago. The initial problem for Liverpool was more their expensive attack was yet to gel.Michael Kayode was keeping Barcola in check and Keane Lewis-Potter was edging his battle with Muñoz. Wirtz was timid and Liverpool’s worries grew when they lost Dominik Szoboszlai to injury.With Ryan Gravenberch suspended, Liverpool were light on midfield options. Trey Nyoni replaced Szoboszali and the 19-year-old’s introduction was followed by a whirlwind spell. Iraola was unhappy when Liverpool had a penalty overturned as replays showed Dango Outtara got a clear touch on the ball before colliding with Alexis Mac Allister.View image in fullscreenYehor Yarmolyuk leaves the pitch after being shown the red card.Photograph: Adam Davy/PABrentford were pumped up after the VAR intervention and soon made Liverpool rue a failure to clear their lines. The ball came back too easily, Mac Allister backed off Thiago, who crossed for Lewis-Potter to run in from left-back and head into the top corner.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We were edging it,” Keith Andrews said. Brentford’s manager wants his team “to play on the edge”, but felt too many decisions went Liverpool’s way. However, he had no complaints about the first red. He said Liverpool were “cute and clever” during the incident, but promised that Yarmolyuk would learn from his mistake.They were into six added minutes at the end of the first half when the midfielder clashed with Jacquet before a Liverpool corner. It was more of a jut than a proper blow, but it was enough to justify the sending off. Brooks checked the pitchside monitor and his decision was not a surprise.Liverpool took a while to adjust in the second half. They encountered further complications when injury forced Jeremie Frimpong off seven minutes after replacing Ronald Araújo at right-back. Mac Allister let fly from distance, but Caoimhín Kelleher saved and Rio Ngumoha, on for Frimpong, crossed for Virgil van Dijk to volley wide.Quick GuideBrentford 1-2 Liverpool key factsShow• Florian Wirtz is the first player to createnine or more chances from open playin a Premier League game since Sadio Mané against Burnley in January 2021 (9), also for Liverpool, and first in an away match since Samir Nasri for Manchester City v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Victor Muñoz (pictured centre, with Wirtz and Trey Nyoni) scored from one of them.• Liverpool’s Alexander Isakhas scored in all fiveof his Premier League appearances against Brentford (5 goals); only Erling Haaland v Crystal Palace (6) has a better 100% rate in the competition.• Brentford received two red cards in the same league game for the first time since April 2013 against Sheffield United in League One.OptaPhotograph: Peter Cziborra/REUTERSWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Brentford began to wobble and they were caught on the counterattack in the 62nd minute. Wirtz dropped back and played a clever pass inside Lewis-Potter. Muñoz raced clear, cut back and drilled a low shot into the far corner with his left foot.The change in mood was dramatic. Barcola sliced a volley just wide, but the winner was coming. Mac Allister took a pass from Wirtz and crossed. Barcola headed down and Isak finished from close range.Iraola was not happy with Liverpool’s play once they led. Brentford threatened an equaliser through Thiago and Liverpool were too rushed. There are flaws to iron out, but this was a positive week for Iraola.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBrentfordLiverpoolmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Boos for Arsenal as draw with Birmingham extends winless WSL run | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Olivia Smith’s strike for Arsenal followed Oceane Hurte’s solo goal in the 1-1 draw to make it five WSL matches without a win for Arsenal
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Olivia Smith’s strike for Arsenal followed Oceane Hurte’s solo goal in the 1-1 draw to make it five WSL matches without a win for Arsenal
Content: Renée Slegers said: ‘I don’t think we created enough in the first half.’Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRenée Slegers said: ‘I don’t think we created enough in the first half.’Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueBoos for Arsenal as draw with Birmingham extends winless WSL runJohn BrewinSat 17 Oct 2026 11.44 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 12.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn equaliser from Olivia Smith averted defeat for Arsenal, but a home draw with Birmingham did little to calm fears for Renée Slegers’s future as Gunners coach. Boos accompanied the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium, as the result left Arsenal on six points from six matches and without a win in five Women’s Super League matches,the club’s longest winless runin WSL history. They are eighth in the table, nine points behind the leaders, Manchester City, who have played one game fewer.Birmingham opened the scoring at the start of the second half when Océane Hurtré coolly tapped in after her run from the halfway line went unchecked. Alessia Russo had hit the woodwork in the first half with a diving header, among a slew of Arsenal chances as Sophie Baggaley was kept the busier of the goalkeepers.The WSL so far: goal-shy Arsenal, underrated Brighton and more data pointersRead more“I don’t think we created enough in the first half,” said Slegers. “Second half is different. There was one player we needed to stop and that was Hurtré. But she came through in a fast break and a counter, we don’t defend that well enough.”After Smith’s spectacular strike, in the 66th minute, curled from outside the area, Arsenal would not find the winning goal that might ease pressure on Slegers. Baggaley’s goalkeeping and slack finishing meant Birmingham secured their point. “We are in a scenario we’ve had too many times season,” said Slegers.Next week for Arsenal is a north London derby with Tottenham, who kick off at Chelsea in fourth on Sunday. Slegers said: “The next game is always the next opportunity. [It’s good] we always keep going and we rise after setbacks.“We just need to put ourselves in better positions earlier so that’s not necessary every time because it takes energy from the team having to play those scenarios. But yes, the team has been brilliant. The urgency, the willingness, the desire in the second half was really good.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDespite those boos at the final whistle, Smith said of the home fans: “They always bring out great support, [we’re] so happy to have them here. Again, disappointed not to get the result, must be frustrating for them, but they stay with us and support us.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueArsenal WomenBirmingham City WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again | Championship | The Guardian
description: West Ham ended Swansea’s four-match winning streak with a 1-0 away victory that reduced the gap at the top of the Championship to a single point
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: West Ham ended Swansea’s four-match winning streak with a 1-0 away victory that reduced the gap at the top of the Championship to a single point
Content: Divine Mukasa celebrates the goal that gave West Ham victory over Swansea.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDivine Mukasa celebrates the goal that gave West Ham victory over Swansea.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesChampionshipChampionship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten againMukasa’s first-half goal enough to beat leaders SwanseaCanaries suffer sixth straight loss; Watford beat CharltonPress AssociationSat 17 Oct 2026 12.29 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 10.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNuno Espírito Santo was delightedWest Hamfinished a “demanding week” by topplingChampionshipleadersSwansea.Divine Mukasa’s first-half strike in front of a record Swansea.com Stadium crowd of 20,973 gave the Hammers a 1-0 win and took them into second place and within a point of the league leaders. It was their second success in four days after a6-0 romp at Lincoln, and ended a week that began with a 1-1 home draw against QPR following Jarrod Bowen’s last-gasp penalty miss.“We wanted not only to keep the momentum, but to build on it,” said Nuno. “It was a very demanding week in terms of the opponents we had to face, but it finished really well due to the hard work of the boys. The commitment, the unity and the way they played was really good against a very good Swansea side. It was a very intense.”Wolves extend Burnley’s home woes to a full year as Vardy strikes in vainRead moreKim Hellberg defended his decision to rest Will Lankshear againstCardiffafter the division’s top scorer came off the bench to rescue a point forMiddlesbrough. Lankshear, who took his tally to 10 for the season in all competitions midweek, was rested him for the visit of the Bluebirds. That selection backfired as Cardiff stunned Boro with two first-half goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner. Lankshear was then introduced at half-time and inspired a fightback, levelling for Boro with his 11th goal of the campaign after Tommy Conway had halved the deficit.View image in fullscreenWill Lankshear’s goal saved a point for Middlesbrough.Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA“You need to manage your players in this league and look into numbers,” said Hellberg. “We have a lot of players that have no pre-season. Will is one of those who came late and has been doing a lot of good things. He’s been absolutely brilliant and sometimes you need to also protect him.”Liam Millar scored twice asBirminghambeatQPR3-0 at St Andrew’s. Millar swung the game Birmingham’s way in the 27th minute and then doubled their advantage just after the break. On both occasions he was assisted by Tomoki Iwata while Demarai Gray added the gloss in the first minute of stoppage time by hammering a pull-back by fellow substitute Luis Vázquez into the top corner.Quick GuideLeague One roundup: Bradford go top; Plymouth loseShowBradfordmoved top of League One with their first home win under Michael Duff, as Plymouth slipped up against Huddersfield. The Bantams, who appointed Duff as manager earlier this month following the departure of Graham Alexander, claimed a 2-0 home win overStevenagethanks to goals inside the last 11 minutes from Antoni Sarcevic and substitute Will Swan. That proved enough to put them a point clear at the top, with previous front-runnersPlymouthgoing down 2-0 at home toHuddersfieldand dropping to fourth in the process. The Terriers climbed above their opponents into third after strikes from Derensili Sanches Fernandez and Bojan Radulovic.Stockportclimbed to second, edging outBromley1-0 with Kyle Wootton on target, while Robbie Savage’s first home league game in charge ofPeterboroughended in a 2-2 draw withBurton. It looked as if Gbemi Arubi’s 89th-minute wonderstrike had earned Albion their first win in three, but Matt Garbett responded with a 96th minute leveller to snatch his side a point. Savage started his time at London Road with a 3-1 win at Leicester last Saturday.Aaron Collins scored the winner asMK DonsbeatLuton2-1 to claim a first league victory of the season. Alex Gilbey fired the Dons ahead with a fine strike before Jordan Clark equalised for the visitors. But Collins’s penalty won the match to condemn Luton to a third defeat in their past four games.Under-pressureLeicestermanager Russell Martin celebrated a badly needed win, seeing off visitingDoncaster2-1 – with Warren O’Hara’s 84th-minute own-goal causing some late tension.Cambridgekept pace with the promotion hopefuls after Shayne Lavery grabbed the winner in added time to leaveBarnsleywith a 2-1 win, whileSheffield Wednesdayeased to a 5-0 win overAFC Wimbledon– Davis Keillor-Dunn with a double.Bottom clubWiganregistered a first league win since 2 September, Scott Hogan with the only goal againstReading.Notts Countylost 2-0 atWycombeandLeyton OrientbeatBlackpool2-0.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Luke Graham scored his first goal forStokeas they won 1-0 at Pride Park to pile more pressure on strugglingDerby. The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest. Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh’s shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.West Bromcompleted a stunning comeback after conceding two early goals as they beatBlackburn3-2. Andri Gudjohnsen had Rovers two up before the break, before Barney Stewart pulled a goal back for Albion. Isaac Price’s penalty levelled it up before the substitute Felix Horn Myhre netted a dramatic winner for the home side a minute from time.James Bree, Lewis Dobbin and Léo Scienza all squandered chances asSouthamptondropped points at home for the first time this season with a 0-0 draw againstBolton. The trio all wasted tap-ins, while Saints were also left bereft by a penalty not being given for a Rúben Rodrigues handball.View image in fullscreenLuca Kjerrumgaard enjoys his crucial opener for Watford against Charlton.Photograph: Ben Peters/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockWatfordlifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggishCharlton. After shipping nine goals in defeats by Burnley and Cardiff,Watfordhad slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as they were booed off at Vicarage Road.Dionisi said later his team was “not yet strong enough for the Championship but it’s possible to improve. I’ve been a coach for 14 years and I know when my team stays near my idea. This result is important and tonight I will drink a glass of red wine.”Portsmouthpiled on the misery for strugglingNorwichas they made it back-to-back Championships victories with a 1-0 win at Carrow Road. Pompey followed up their midweek victory againstSheffield Unitedwith a hard-fought success in East Anglia, with a 51st-minute penalty from striker Marezi settling the issue.It was a sixth successive league defeat for the hosts and there were calls for the sporting director Ben Knapper to go from frustrated supporters at the final whistle.Norwich’s head coach, Philippe Clement, had no complaints with his side’s effort – but felt they sometimes failed to see the bigger picture on the pitch.“I am very disappointed, very frustrated,” he said. “I saw a lot of passion out there, a lot of effort, but not enough overview. It’s about getting the balance right between their hearts and their brains. I understand the frustration of our fans and all I can say is that I will work even harder than I did last season to turn it around.”View image in fullscreenPortsmouth’s Marezi celebrates on another bleak day for Norwich.Photograph: Stephen Pond/Getty ImagesJake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point forMillwallas they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 withLincoln. The visitors looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. ButMillwallwere able to prevent back-to-back home defeats with a much-improved second-half performance, and the visitors were hanging on for a share of the spoils after having Deji Elerewe sent off soon after Cooper’s leveller. Kyrell Lisbie had scored Millwall’s first.Quick GuideLeague Two roundup: Salford make it five in a rowShowLeague Two pacesettersSalfordmade it five wins in a row in the fourth tier as Macaulay Langstaff scored twice in a 2-1 success over bottom sideCrawley. Barnet and Crewe remain close by just a point further back.Barnetcame from behind to beatTranmere2-1, Kabongo Tshimanga scoring both, andCrewedefeatedRochdale3-2.Yorkwere held to a 1-1 draw atNewportafter going down to 10 men butShrewsburyheld on 1-0 againstBristol Roversdespite two red cards in the last 10 minutes.Ian Holloway’sSwindonare now eight games without a win in all competitions after a 1-1 draw withWalsall,Oldhameased to a 4-1 result againstCheltenhamandPort ValeedgedChesterfield1-0.Ten-manGrimsbywent down 2-0 toNorthampton,Accringtontook a 3-1 win overGillingham, strugglersRotherhamlost 2-0 atFleetwoodand there was a goalless draw betweenColchesterandExeter.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Oliver Arblaster’s early strike and a strong defensive display sawSheffield Unitedtake all three points from a 1-0 victory overBristol Cityat Ashton Gate. The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave the City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance. It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.Wrexhameased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a 4-1 win over rock-bottomPreston. Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, the former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal inWrexhamcolours. Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.In a week that had seen former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard linked with the manager’s job, Wrexham’s third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th. But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipWest Ham UnitedSwansea CityWatfordMiddlesbroughCardiff CityMillwallnewsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Rangers miss chance to go top after pulsating draw with Dundee | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Rangers passed up the chance to go top in a pulsating 2-2 draw at Dundee, while Kilmarnock beat Motherwell 3-2 to move off the bottom
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Rangers passed up the chance to go top in a pulsating 2-2 draw at Dundee, while Kilmarnock beat Motherwell 3-2 to move off the bottom
Content: Bradley Fink gives Dundee a first-half lead against Rangers at Dens Park.Photograph: Zak Mauger/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBradley Fink gives Dundee a first-half lead against Rangers at Dens Park.Photograph: Zak Mauger/Getty ImagesScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Rangers miss chance to go top after pulsating draw with DundeeJones equaliser denies Rangers victoryKilmarnock beat Motherwell 3-2 to move off bottomPress AssociationSat 17 Oct 2026 17.33 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 13.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRangerspassed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw againstDundeeat Dens Park. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level.Dundeewere well worth a point, with Rangers moving one point behind Celtic, who can increase their lead at home to Hearts on Sunday.European football: Barcelona thrash Real Betis to maintain 100% recordRead moreGreg Kiltie scored twice to liftKilmarnockoff the bottom with a 3-2 home victory overMotherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.View image in fullscreenGreg Kiltie celebrates scoring his second goal against Motherwell, which proved to be Kilmarnock’s winner.Photograph: Mark Runnacles/ShutterstockMotherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”Falkirksecured an entertaining 2-1 win atHibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell putFalkirk2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.Aberdeenreturned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory overSt Mirrenmoved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earnedDundee Uniteda 1-1 draw atSt Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipAberdeenSt MirrenHibernianFalkirkKilmarnockMotherwellnewsShareReuse this content

title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Pedro Neto scored twice in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton in a game which saw goalkeeper Emi Martínez carried off on a stretcher with a head injury
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Pedro Neto scored twice in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton in a game which saw goalkeeper Emi Martínez carried off on a stretcher with a head injury
Content: Chelsea's Emi Martínez and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite clash heads going for the ball.Photograph: Peter Powell/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChelsea's Emi Martínez and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite clash heads going for the ball.Photograph: Peter Powell/AFP/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueNeto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injuryAndy Hunterat Hill Dickinson StadiumSat 17 Oct 2026 09.53 EDTLast modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 11.23 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine.The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A firstPremier Leagueclean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance.Everton v Chelsea: Premier League – liveRead more“It’s one day,” the Chelsea manager replied when asked whether victory, built on a feisty first-half display and mature second, provided evidence of the mentality he craves at Stamford Bridge. “We need to repeat it again and again and again to know for sure but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it’s not about playing nice but playing good football, winning many second balls and being efficient. We need a game like this. The feeling at Brentford was that it was not enough. Today has been better but it’s just one. When it’s 10 clean sheets …”There were goalkeeping problems at both ends of the field, with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in a row forEverton. David Moyes’s side edged the first half and could have legitimate complaints about Morgan Rogers avoiding a second yellow card moments before the break. But from Pickford’s weak attempt to stop Neto’s opener to Thierno Barry missing their one big chance of the contest, there were self-inflicted wounds in Everton’s first defeat of the season.“It wasn’t that we played that badly overall,” said Moyes. “We just didn’t create enough which meant if we did anything wrong defensively it would count against us.” So it proved.There was more needle than quality in the first half and Rogers, already booked, was extremely fortunate to avoid a second yellow card from the referee, Paul Tierney, when leaping into a challenge with James Garner. The Chelsea forward caught the ball and the man. The tackle could be considered just as reckless as the one that brought an earlier booking for Harrison Armstrong.Barry wasted Everton’s best chance when heading a Jack Grealish cross straight at Martínez from close range. Another big miss from Barry was one of several recurring themes that undermined Everton’s afternoon.View image in fullscreenPedro Neto shows his delight after giving Chelsea the lead.Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesChelsea began to contain the hosts and turn the tide as the interval approached. They were inches away from taking the lead in spectacular fashion. Moisés Caicedo pulled away to the back post for a Jordan Henderson corner that arrived exactly where the training ground routine required. His thunderous volley flew past Pickford but smacked the crossbar, leaving it shaking for several seconds.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNeto forced a decent save from the Everton keeper from distance in first-half stoppage time and beat him from much closer range 44 seconds after the restart. As in the draw at Hull last weekend, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Pickford were found wanting defensively. Rogers was somewhat inevitably involved when releasing Jorrel Hato, Alonso’s one enforced change from the 5-1 defeat of Bournemouth, away from Maitland-Niles down the Chelsea left. Hato’s cross took a fortunate touch off James Tarkowski en route to Neto, whose shot beat Pickford’s weak attempt to save low to his left.Goalkeeping worries took on a far more serious complexion when Branthwaite collided with Martínez as they challenged for a Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall free-kick. The Chelsea keeper required lengthy treatment before being carried away with his neck in a brace and to the uncomfortable sound of Evertonian boos. Thankfully he gave a thumbs up to Branthwaite when the concerned Everton defender waited to wish him well.Martínez’s replacement, Mike Penders on his Premier League debut, was not seriously tested as the Everton threat petered out and Chelsea maintained control of the second half. Victory was sealed in the final minute of normal time when Henderson’s free-kick struck the head of Barry, rebounded off the Everton substitute Tyrique George and Vitalii Mykolenko, before dropping to Neto. The Chelsea winger rolled a confident finish past Pickford’s despairing dive into the bottom corner.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueEvertonChelseamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith  | Australia cricket team | The Guardian
description: Kagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood as the South Africa bowler prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve Smith
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood as the South Africa bowler prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve Smith
Content: Kagiso Rabada during a South Africa training session. The quick will return from injury to face Australia in the second Test in Gqeberha.Photograph: Darren Stewart/Gallo Images/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKagiso Rabada during a South Africa training session. The quick will return from injury to face Australia in the second Test in Gqeberha.Photograph: Darren Stewart/Gallo Images/Getty ImagesAustralia cricket team‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith‘There’s no hate,’ says bowler ahead of return to St George’s ParkPair clashed in Gqeberha during heated series six years agoAustralian Associated PressSat 17 Oct 2026 19.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood with Australia as the South Africa speedster prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve Smith.Rabada has been declared fit to come back from his hamstring tear and face Australia in the second Test at St George’s Park, in his first match since May. The South African’s return comes at a crucial point in the series, with the hosts fighting to stay alive after their 214-run pumping in Durban last week.The Spin | The sleepy English hotel where Bradman and Australia left cricket memories galoreRead moreBut it is also timely, given it was at St George’s Park where Rabada was initially banned for two Tests for colliding with Smith while celebrating taking his wicket in 2018.Rabada ultimately had his ban downgraded to a fine, leaving Smith and Australia unhappy that the batter was not able to speak at the hearing. The shoulder bump, and ensuing appeal, was one of the final flash points of the ill-spirited series before the ball-tampering scandal overshadowed it all.View image in fullscreenRabada celebrates taking the wicket of Smith in 2018.Photograph: Mike Hutchings/ReutersRabada has played against Australia 23 times across all formats since then without issue, while also being a teammate to some in franchise leagues. Speaking to local media before Sunday’s return, the 31-year-old made it clear he had no ill will towards Smith, even if he couldn’t see the pair meeting for coffee.“That is just the emotion of the game. It’s about playing within the rules,” Rabada said. “As an athlete you want to go out and express yourself. There’s no hate off the field or anything like that. It’s a bunch of top-performing athletes who’ve got testosterone to burn. It’s the heat of the moment.“But, with the ICC, you have to take into consideration the rules that have been put in place regarding viewers who are watching the game, and keeping the game in a good light. That’s understandable. You need characters in sport. But you also need to play within the rules.”Smith’s wicket was the first of 11 Rabada took for the match at St George’s Park in 2018, on his way to being man of the series. The right-armer also has the second best record of any quick against Australia this century, with his 58 wickets at 21.39 behind only India’s Jasprit Bumrah.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“He’ll obviously feed off the performances that he’s had against Australia,” captain Temba Bavuma said. “The bowlers, they feed massively over him. He leads the attack in everything that he does. And then I think he brings an extra level of confidence to the unit.“You mentioned the aura. There’s a lot of belief in KG, and a lot of the guys rub off there. He’s raring to go.”South Africa will wait until Sunday to decide their final side, with rain predicted for the opening day and both teams preparing for a shortened Test. The Proteas have already confirmed Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne will be dropped, with Marques Ackerman and Matthew Breetzke expected to come in.Explore more on these topicsAustralia cricket teamSouth Africa cricket teamCricketAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Daniel Dubois knocks out Fabio Wardley to retain WBO heavyweight title – as it happened | Boxing | The Guardian
