Author: Alex Reid
Headline: Daniel Dubois demolished Fabio Wardley inside five minutes at London’s O2 Arena
Content: 2h ago18.39 EDTFight reportDonald McRaeDaniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in the second round of their WBO world title fight on Saturday nightas he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet with this crushing victory. This was the second time in five months that Dubois has defeated Wardley but, after theirfight of the year contender in May, this was a shockingly one-sided shellacking.After two minutes and 21 seconds of round two, Wardley was rescued from the bludgeoning fists of Dubois by the referee, just as the fluttering white towel of his trainer, Ben Davison, sailed over the ropes in surrender.Daniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO titleRead moreShare

title: Atlanta Dream 64-68 Golden State Valkyries: WNBA finals 2026 Game 1 – as it happened | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Minute-by-minute report: The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream in the opening game of the WNBA finals. Bryan Graham was watching
Author: Bryan Armen Graham
Headline: Minute-by-minute report: The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream in the opening game of the WNBA finals. Bryan Graham was watching
Content: 17.53 EDTFinal: Dream 64-68 ValkyriesGabby Williams scored 26 points as theGolden State Valkyriesrallied to beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA finals on Saturday, taking a 1-0 lead in the best-of-seven series.Williams, who went scoreless in the opening quarter, erupted for 16 points in the second to erase an eight-point deficit before delivering four crucial free throws in the final minutes.Atlanta led 22-14 after the first quarter behind Angel Reese’s dominant start, but Golden State responded with a 28-point second period. The Dream regained control in the third, only to come apart offensively down the stretch.The Dream managed just eight points in the fourth quarter, shooting two-for-19 from the field and missing all seven three-point attempts. Allisha Gray, who led the Dream with 19 points, went scoreless in the final period.Reese finished with 14 points and 12 rebounds – going scoreless after half-time – while Rhyne Howard added 12.Kiah Stokes contributed nine points, seven rebounds and four blocks for Golden State, who prevailed despite shooting just 32.1% from the field before a sellout crowd of 18,064 at Chase Center.Golden State’s Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points in Game 1 of the WNBA finals.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesShareUpdated at18.00 EDT

title: European football: Barcelona thrash Real Betis to maintain 100% record | European club football | The Guardian
description: Barcelona won 5-2 at Real Betis to maintain their five-point La Liga lead with a ninth straight victory, while Bayern Munich thumped RB Leipzig 6-1
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Barcelona won 5-2 at Real Betis to maintain their five-point La Liga lead with a ninth straight victory, while Bayern Munich thumped RB Leipzig 6-1
Content: Gabriel Jesus (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona's third goal with Lamine Yamal.Photograph: Jorge Guerrero/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenGabriel Jesus (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona's third goal with Lamine Yamal.Photograph: Jorge Guerrero/AFP/Getty ImagesEuropean club footballEuropean football: Barcelona thrash Real Betis to maintain 100% recordLamine Yamal opens scoring in ninth straight winLuis Díaz hat-trick helps Bayern thump RB Leipzig 6-1AgenciesSat 17 Oct 2026 17.33 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 10.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBarcelona’s La Liga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beatReal Betis5-2 to make it ⁠nine wins from nine, ⁠stretching their blistering league ​goal tally to 39.Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric García and the substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentín Gómez and Ez Abde replied ⁠for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for head-butting Lamine Yamal.Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gómez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan García.Barcelona reclaimed the lead on 41 minutes when ‌the Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermín López’s corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso’s spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho ​Hernández was adjudged to have handled.Jesus had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine Yamal darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly.A minute later Abde pulled one back on the counter, sliding a low shot inside the right post, but Betis’ celebrations turned ⁠sour when Bernal was shown a straight red card following a scuffle. Lamine Yamal was booked for ​his part in the altercation.Barcelona made it 4-2 ​in the 63rd minute when Álvaro Valles failed ​to deal with Lamine Yamal’s free-kick and Pau Cubarsi headed the loose ball back across goal for García ​to tap in.View image in fullscreenÁlex Baena celebrates scoring Atlético Madrid’s late winner against Espanyol.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersÁlex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch a 1-0 win forAtlético MadridatEspanyol.Baena smashed in from the edge of the box to claim theRojiblancosvictory from a tight game in Cornella. Atlético have won six consecutive games across all competitions and remain five points behind Barcelona.ValenciaandAthletic Bilbaodrew 0-0.On Sunday fourth-placed Real Madrid, nine points behind Barça with a game in hand, host Sevilla. In the buildup to that game, theReal Madridcoach, José Mourinho, said on Saturday that if he wereVinícius Júniorhe would have left the club this summer. The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid’s win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss theclásicoagainst Barcelona on 25 October.Vinícius, who signed a new contract tying him toReal Madriduntil 2032, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018.“He’s a spectacular kid who it’s easy to have a good relationship with,” Mourinho said. “He’s a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile ... If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn’t be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him.”Mourinho took Vinícius off during the 4-3 Champions League win atRomaon Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to find the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti. Mourinho said he was happy that Vinícius’s ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee “would give him one or two more”.In Germany, Luis Díaz scored a hat-trick asBayern Munichpummelled a listlessRB Leipzig6-1 at home to climb to the top of the Bundesliga table.Borussia Dortmundhad edged ahead ofFreiburginto top spot after their earlier goalless draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion.The dominant display was Bayern’s best performance of the season and will boost their confidence before Wednesday’s home Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal.View image in fullscreenLuis Díaz fires Bayern Munich into the lead.Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPADíaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life to terrorise the Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left. In his 100thBundesligamatch, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet. Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1.In Italy,Interpulled clear at the top of Serie A by coming from behind to beatBologna3-1. The champions were criticised after a 4-3 Champions League defeat against Club Brugge in midweek, but bounced back to move three points clear of second-placed Lazio, who face Juventus in Turin on Sunday.Bologna started brightly at the Stadio Renato Dall’Ara as Tommaso Pobega fired them in front after 10 minutes before hitting the bar with a powerful shot. But Inter, shorn of their injured top scorer and captain, Lautaro Martínez, after he was ruled out for a month, responded through a towering Marcus Thuram header and would have gone in at the break in front were it not for a superb Lukasz Skorupski save from Francesco Pio Esposito. Carlos Augusto scored within a minute of coming on midway through the second half, before turning provider for his fellow replacement Ange-Yoan Bonny late on.Romadispatched Genoa 2-0 to move into second. With their top-scorer, Donyell Malen, suspended and several key players injured, Roma’s youngsters seized their chance as Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli scored their first goals for the club. Genoa’s coach, Daniele De Rossi, a celebrated former Roma player and coach, received a warm ovation from the home support but was unable to prevent his counterpart, Gian Piero Gasperini, from claiming the 300thSerie Awin of his managerial career.Napoli’s torrid start to the season continued whenVenezia’s head coach, Davide Nicola, masterminded a shock 1-0 win in his first game as Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved. Nicola was appointed during the week to replace Giovanni Stroppa after last season’s Serie B champions failed to pick up a single point in their opening six games. He made an instant impact as Akor Adams struck the winner early in the second half to seal Venezia’s first Serie A win over Napoli since 1942.View image in fullscreenVenezia’s Filip Stankovic saves the penalty from Napoli’s Kevin De Bruyne.Photograph: Matteo Ciambelli/ReutersIn France, Ousmane Dembélé missed a penalty but later scored asParis Saint-Germainproduced a fightback to win 3-1 atStrasbourgand go top of the Ligue 1 table.PSG were trailing to an early goal by Giovanni Reyna at the Stade de la Meinau, and last year’s Ballon d’Or winner then put a penalty wide in the 72nd minute. But Dembélé made amends in style, first by setting up Illia Zabarnyi to equalise in the 78th minute and then by putting the reigning French and European champions ahead with five minutes to go.He then played a part in setting up Désiré Doué for PSG’s third in stoppage time, as Luis Enrique’s men made it four straightLigue 1wins, and six on the bounce including the Champions League.After failing to win any of their first three domestic league matches this season, PSG are up to 14 points from seven games and are therefore top of the standings on goals scored from Monaco, before the principality club visit Lorient on Sunday. Lille, Rennes, Paris FC and Lyon all have the opportunity to go back above PSG in the table over the weekend.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballLa LigaAtlético MadridReal MadridEspanyolVinícius JúniorJosé MourinhonewsShareReuse this content

title: Champions Cup roundup: La Rochelle beat Lions after emotional tribute to Andrews | Champions Cup | The Guardian
description: After both team remembered the Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who was found dead on Friday, La Rochelle beat the Johannesburg side 31-14
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: After both team remembered the Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who was found dead on Friday, La Rochelle beat the Johannesburg side 31-14
Content: Players from both teams observed a minute of silence in tribute to Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday, at his hotel.Photograph: Yohan Bonnet/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenPlayers from both teams observed a minute of silence in tribute to Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday, at his hotel.Photograph: Yohan Bonnet/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockChampions CupChampions Cup roundup: La Rochelle beat Lions after emotional tribute to AndrewsLions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, found dead on FridayConnacht 45-36 Saracens; Sale 27-47 GlasgowAgence France-Press and Press AssociationSat 17 Oct 2026 17.33 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 10.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Johannesburg-basedLionsput up a gritty fight on an emotionalChampions Cupdebut but came up short 31-14 atLa Rochelleas both sides paid tribute to the South African lock Hyron Andrews, who died suddenly at the team’s hotel in western France.The whole stadium observed a minute’s silence while Andrews’s No 5 shirt was laid on the pitch before kick-off. La Rochelle’s three South African players presented a jersey to their visitors in memory of the player, who died on Friday at Lions’ hotel on the nearby Ile de Ré. A source close to the investigation said thatAndrews, who was 31, was found in cardiac arrestin a shower cubicle that was locked from the inside.The wingers Tevita Ofa and Davit Niniashvili were on the scoresheet in the first half for hostsLa Rochelle, who led 19-14 as Lions replied through Henco van Wyk and Morné Brandon. Second-half scores from Australia hooker Silatolu Latu and Fijian winger Avakuki Niusalelekitoga earned La Rochelle a bonus point.In the other game in Pool 2, Cian Prendergast and Ciaran Frawley scored two tries apiece asConnachtdefeatedSaracens45-36 in a thriller. Saracens made the better start and opened up a 12-0 lead through tries from Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori but the Irish side came storming back.View image in fullscreenSaracens’ Noah Caluori (centre) is tackled by Connacht’s Daniel Ryan.Photograph: Brian Lawless/PAThree tries in 12 minutes from Prendergast, Cathal Forde and Shamus Hurley-Langton put them in front, but the latter was sent to the sin-bin just before half-time and Nick Tompkins capitalised to make it 19-19 at the break. It remained nip and tuck as Prendergast went over for his second only for Rotimi Segun to find a swift reply. Frawley was next to cross before Vaenuku grabbed his second but tries from Caolin Blade and Frawley’s second helped Connacht open up a 14-point gap.That was reduced to nine when Elliot Daly scored Saracens’ sixth try following a yellow card for Prendergast but Owen Farrell missed the conversion to deny them a bonus point.Glasgow Warriorsextended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win atSalein Pool 1. Glasgow’s winning score looked convincing, but they secured victory in the final 20 minutes after Rekeiti Ma’asi-White had temporarily reduced Sale’s deficit to four.View image in fullscreenRekeiti Ma’asi-White of Sale Sharks points to the sky in celebration after scoring a try.Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Sale SharksThe hosts had made all the running in the early stages and were 12 points up inside the first 10 minutes thanks to tries from Ben Curry and Arron Reed. The visitors hit back through a penalty try and further efforts from Kyle Steyn and Jamie Dobie to carve out a 21-15 lead at the interval.The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Tavi Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a bonus-point win. Glasgow host Pau in their next Champions Cup encounter while Sale travel toLeinsterfor a tricky test in mid-December.Also in Pool 1,Leinsterproduced a fine second-half display as the Irish side recorded a bonus-point 48-23 win againstClermontat the Stade Marcel-Michelin.Tadhg Furlong and Dan Sheehan both scored tries for Leinster in the opening period, but the visitors trailed 16-15 at the interval after a Joris Jurand try and 11 points from Harry Plummer’s boot. Sam Prendergast crossed for Leinster moments after the half-time break and they took full control when Clermont collapsed a scrum which handed the visitors a penalty try and led to Nohem Ez Zahouany being sent to the sin-bin.Leinster quickly took advantage of their numerical superiority as Sheehan touched down for his second try of the afternoon. Mathys Belaubre crossed for Clermont’s second try of the day, Jack Conan quickly responded with a converted score that gave Leinster a 20-point advantage when the penalty expired. Tommy O’Brien’s 76th-minute try then added gloss to the score as the Irish side wrapped up an impressive victory on French soil.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn Pool 3, theStormersran in seven tries in a 49-12 thumping ofBristolin their Champions Cup opener. The home side were on top from the start in Cape Town, with Seabelo Senatla scoring their first try in the seventh minute before Leolin Zas added a second eight minutes later.Joe Owen broke away down the wing for a solo try for Bristol in the 22nd minute but Jonny Roche restored Stormers’ advantage before the half-hour mark. JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card for head-to-head contact before the break, while a yellow card for Zas – resulting in a disallowed try – gave the Bears a significant numerical advantage that they took advantage of through a first try for the club from Sol Moody.However, Roche then scored his second and the final 10 minutes was a horror show for Bristol as they conceded three more tries. First, Warrick Gelant crossed, then Andre-Hugo Venter got in on the act before Vas ended an eventful game with his second – with all seven tries converted by Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.Also in Pool 3, Brian Gleeson paid the perfect tribute to the late Anthony Foley, relinquishing the No 8 jersey then scoringMunster’sopening try in a 33-25 win overRacing 92. The No 8 jersey was retired for the night at Supervalu Pairc ui Chaoimh in honour of the club’s former captain and head coach, who died aged 42 on the eve of a clash between the same teams in 2016.Gleeson instead wore No 24 and gave the Irish side a seventh-minute lead when he powered over the line. That helped his side take a 14-6 half-time lead, Shay McCarthy adding a second score. Both teams touched down three times in an expansive second half, Tadhg Beirne, Fineen Wychereley and Craig Casey for the hosts, who never surrendered the lead, while Wilfried Hulleu, Maxime Machenaud and Joey Manu responded for the French team. Charlie O’Shea converted three times on debut and Antoine Gibert kicked 10 points in a losing cause.In Pool 4, theBullsbeatStadeFrançais21-6, whileBathwere dealt a second-half lesson byMontpellieras they fell to a 32-14 defeat at The Rec. The home side led 14-10 at the interval after Ollie Lawrence and Arthur Green both scored tries following Stuart Hogg’s opener.However, Joe Cokanasiga then wasted a golden opportunity to extend Bath’s advantage after the interval and the French side capitalised. Donovan Taofifenua crossed in the corner to give Montpellier the lead before he then intercepted Finn Russell’s pass to deliver a quickfire double. Alex Becognee made the points safe for the visiting side after Josh Bayliss’s try forBathwas ruled out because of an earlier infringement.Explore more on these topicsChampions CupSaleGlasgow RugbyStade FrançaisBullsRugby unionLeinsternewsShareReuse this content
